task.summary:
Update function documentation and user guide in README
The update significantly improves the documentation for several functions in 'app.py', providing a much clearer understanding of their operation. The README.md file's instructions for app deployment and usage have also been modified to suit the specific features of the BML Payment Integration application.

Update README to reflect BML Payment Integration
The existing README content has been replaced with specific instructions and details about the deployment and usage of the BML Payment Integration application. It now includes clearer setup steps, the necessary environment variables, and a description of how the application handles transactions.

Refactor code and update comments in `app.py`
Code has been restructured for better readability and to improve efficiency in `app.py`. Comment documentation for methods has been revised for clarity, with some discrepancies in method labels corrected and unnecessary details removed. Route mappings and error handling have been improved within some methods.

Add student creation in Xperiencify platform and remove test_app file
This update includes the creation of a new student in the Xperiencify platform whenever a payment confirmation from BML is received. This action requires an Experiencify API key. If it's not available or an invalid magic link is generated, the user will be redirected to a default URL. The `test_app.py` file has been removed as it's no longer necessary and new exceptions have been added to handle invalid magic links. In the subscription module, functionalities to retrieve customer and product details have also been added.

Refactor code indentation for student creation logic
The student creation if condition has been realigned to improve readability in the app.py file. This change ensures the logic for creation using the "Experiencify" API key is more readable, and consistent with other code blocks.

Update error handling and return order in subscription.py
The exception handling logic in 'checkoutpage' API request has been improved to better handle unsuccessful API responses. Additionally, the order of return from 'invoice_data' has been altered from (customer_id, product_id) to (product_id, customer_id) for alignment with other parts of the code.

Refactor code to use passed API key
The function load_dotenv and the variable API_KEY were removed from the code as they were not necessary. Instead, the API key is now directly passed to the required functions as a string. This makes the code much cleaner and reduces dependencies on external variables or processes.

Refactor course ID verification in redirect.py
The verification check for course IDs has been enhanced in redirect.py. The updated code now explicitly checks within the dictionary keys for a matching course ID. Additionally, the generation of the string of course IDs has been altered for better readability and clarity.

Refactor create_student function in redirect.py
This change clarifies data types for create_student function parameters and refactors the way course_ids are compiled to be more efficient. The course title is now specifically converted to a string to prevent possible type-related issues.

Update magic link validation in redirect.py
The magic link validation condition in the redirect.py module has been updated. The code now checks if the magic link starts with "https:" instead of a specific URL. Furthermore, if the link is not valid, it raises an InvalidMagicLink exception instead of returning an error message.

Simplify URL verification for student creation
The previous check for https:// at the beginning of the redirect URL inside the try block of create_student function was removed. Now the code only logs an error and defaults to DEFAULT_REDIRECT_URL if the URL does not start with https://. This makes the logic easier to follow.

Add redirection logging in app.py
An error_logging call has been added to log the final redirection url. This change provides visibility into where the user is being redirected to after an action is performed.

Rename variable for clarity in redirect.py
The variable 'course_id' in the redirect.py script has been renamed to 'course_identifier'. This change has been made to improve code readability and make the variable's purpose more explicit. Now its use throughout the rest of the code will be more intuitive.

Remove json sample files and helpers.py script
Removed unnecessary JSON sample files and a Python script named 'helpers.py'. These were either unused or obsolete, which did not contribute to the main action of the application. The removal helps to reduce clutter and improve maintainability of the project.
